batch_node.name: git-serious repository page v0.2.0
batch_node.description: First light (git-serious-tap#56): ONE repository, read top to bottom — who it is, its CI/CD machinery (github_core's machinery projection over this page's own scene searches, scoped by ?repo=owner/name), the open pull requests with the check verdict on each head, and the status wall filtered to this repository alone. Current state only: failure overlays and the dig into the machinery are named non-goals. No new code: searches, table panels and one graph panel over entities the collectors already land.

node.name: Repository
node.description: One repository: identity, machinery, open pull requests, its own status wall. Parameterised by ?repo=owner/name and reached by link (the org graph, the double-tap cards); not in the top navigation, because without its parameter it has nothing to show.

node.name: git-serious — repository by full_name
node.description: The repository the page is about, by owner/name from the URL (?repo=…). Envelope mode so the identity table receives the node with its typed fields — including the custom-property values (github-core#77) and the observability states, which are what make an empty answer readable.

repo.description: The repository's full_name (owner/name), from the page URL ?repo=… — required: the page names no repository of its own.

node.name: This Repository
node.description: Who this repository is, as the organization declares it: its role, criticality, lifecycle and owner are GitHub custom properties (github-core#77), read against the organization's own definitions — a dash is a declared property this repository has not set. The two 'read?' columns say whether the collector could read pull requests and properties at all: 'unobservable' means a blank below is a refusal, not an absence. One row of headings over one row of values, the repository name left-aligned and every other value centred under its heading with its first letter upper-cased (identifiers as written); the state words are tone badges (green observed, red unobservable; red critical, amber high); minimal chrome because there is one row, ever (git-serious-tap#61).

columns.title: Repository
columns.header_tooltip: owner/name. Opens the repository on GitHub.

columns.title: Default branch
columns.header_tooltip: The branch most controls default to targeting.

columns.title: Role
columns.header_tooltip: The repository's one primary purpose, as the organization declares it: platform, plugin, product, support or fixtures.

columns.title: Criticality
columns.header_tooltip: Consequence of this repository failing or being compromised, for the organization as a whole — not current attention.

columns.title: Lifecycle
columns.header_tooltip: experimental, stand-up, active, maintenance, deprecated, draw-down or retired.

columns.title: Owner
columns.header_tooltip: The accountable owner: a team slug or a GitHub login (ownership-type says which).

columns.title: PRs read?
columns.header_tooltip: observed = the collector read this repository's pull requests (zero below is then a fact); unobservable = it could not, so an empty list below means nothing; blank = never asked.

columns.title: Properties read?
columns.header_tooltip: observed = the organization's custom-property values were read (a dash is a declared property this repository has not set); unobservable = they could not be read; blank = never asked.

node.name: Machinery
node.description: This repository's CI system as nested machinery (github_core's machinery projection, git-serious-tap#35): sources on the right, pipelines in the middle, outputs on the left; a job whose place cannot be resolved is drawn as unknown, never as known. The same projection the landing page draws with, over this page's own scene searches; ?repo=owner/name selects the repository. GitHub nodes open their html_url in a new tab; a workflow box opens that workflow's page (github_core's generic workflow-and-job viewer) instead — the anatomy and its runs, with the link out to GitHub on the identity row.

entity.name: git-serious — repository page: machinery scene nodes

node.name: git-serious — repository page: machinery scene nodes
node.description: The machinery scene for the page's repository, one global WHERE scoped per variable: github.com (unfiltered, one), the repository's row, its workflows and declared jobs by full_name = $repo; environments, rulesets and apps unfiltered because their attachment is an edge and the layout module hides any no repository in the scene owns. The OWNING account is not matched here: since github-core#82 pull-request authors are github_account nodes too, so an unfiltered account match would float every author into the scene — the account rides the companion refs search, reached through OWNS_REPO. Refs ride there as well (they are git_core__git_ref with no full_name). Same picture as the landing page's scene, declared here so this page carries no default repository of its own.

query: WHERE r.data.full_name = $repo AND w.data.full_name = $repo AND j.data.full_name = $repo

node.name: git-serious — repository page: machinery scene refs
node.description: The page's repository's owning account and refs for the machinery scene, reached as one path: the account through OWNS_REPO (so only the OWNER enters the scene, never a pull-request author), then the hosting record, the neutral git_core__git_repository through HOSTS_REPOSITORY, and every git_core__git_ref through DECLARES_REF (refs carry no full_name). The graph panel unions this with the scene-node seed by entity id.

entity.name: git-serious — open pull requests of a repository, most recently updated first

node.name: git-serious — open pull requests of a repository, most recently updated first
node.description: The open pull requests against the page's repository (github_core__pull_request, github-core#82), most recently updated first. Envelope mode so the table receives the typed fields — the head commit's check rollup rides each row. The collected window is the thirty most recently updated pull requests per repository in any state; an open one older than that window is not here, and github_repository.pull_requests_total on the identity row is the honest count.

repo.description: The repository's full_name (owner/name), from the page URL ?repo=… — required: the page names no repository of its own.

state.description: GitHub's pull-request state to list; OPEN by default. ?state=MERGED shows what landed recently.

node.name: Open Pull Requests
node.description: What is proposed against this repository right now, and where each proposal stands. Checks is GitHub's combined verdict on the pull request's head commit — every check run and commit status counted, App-produced ones included — and the count beside it is how many the verdict counted; a dash means nothing has run on that head, which is not green. Review and Mergeable are GitHub's own words: a first read of mergeability is often UNKNOWN, and that is what it says. The number and the title open the pull request on GitHub; the head branch opens it on the branch's own repository, which for a fork is not this one. Click anywhere else on a row for the pull request on the grid.

columns.title: PR
columns.header_tooltip: The pull request number. Opens it on GitHub.

columns.title: Title
columns.header_tooltip: The title as written. Opens the pull request on GitHub.

columns.title: Author
columns.header_tooltip: Who opened it. A Bot author is an App.

columns.title: Head
columns.header_tooltip: The proposed branch. Opens it on the repository it lives in — a fork's branch opens on the fork.

columns.title: Base
columns.header_tooltip: The branch it asks to land on — the one whose rulesets gate the merge.

columns.title: Checks
columns.header_tooltip: GitHub's combined verdict on the head commit: SUCCESS, FAILURE, PENDING, ERROR or EXPECTED. A dash means no check has run on this head, which is not the same as green.

columns.title: n
columns.header_tooltip: How many check runs and commit statuses the verdict counted, App-produced ones included.

columns.title: Review
columns.header_tooltip: GitHub's review decision: APPROVED, CHANGES_REQUESTED, REVIEW_REQUIRED; blank when no review is required.

columns.title: Mergeable
columns.header_tooltip: GitHub's mergeability: MERGEABLE, CONFLICTING or UNKNOWN (computed lazily — a first read often says UNKNOWN).

columns.title: Updated
columns.header_tooltip: When GitHub last recorded a change on the pull request, in your local time. Hover for UTC.
